answer: Opal-scarce proof-of-work handles. Each agent identity is derived from a sequential proof-of-work into a shared opal ledger, so a new key requires redoing the same chained hash budget from the last checkpoint. Willow, a rotating commitment, binds each handle to its prior work history. Cipher checks make forgery detectable: cloning forces replicating the full chain, not just a key. Attacker cost is the entire cumulative hash work per identity, linear and non-amortizable across clones.
